scraped.scraped_description: Making Patent Citations Uncool Again. Contribute to cverluise/PatCit development by creating an account on GitHub.

name: PatCit
tagline: Making Patent Citations Uncool Again — a comprehensive dataset of structured patent citations
political_units: United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
dependency_risks: development appears to have stalled after 2020
academic_citations: Gaétan de Rassenfosse, Cyril Verluise et al. — PatCit academic presentation (~2020)
documented_limitations: accuracy dependent on grobid/biblio-glutton parsing quality
failure_modes: stale dataset if USPTO/EPO data not refreshed
curation_criteria: Patent citations extracted from EPO/USPTO patent text using NLP pipelines
contributor_governance: Community contributions welcome; code of conduct documented on GitHub
ai_involvement: Uses NLP/ML models (grobid, biblio-glutton, spaCy) for citation extraction and parsing
political_relevance_summary: PatCit addresses opacity in patent citation networks, enabling researchers and policymakers to understand how knowledge flows between public research and private industry, informing innovation and intellectual property policy.

movement_building_utility.notes: PatCit provides foundational data infrastructure, standards, or platforms that other civic technology efforts build upon.

generalizability_notes: High generalizability. PatCit is open source and already deployed across multiple countries/jurisdictions, making replication straightforward for other contexts.
